question: We have the registry of subjects who are vaccinated against the flu in a specific region and campaign, which includes information at the time of vaccination on pathological history, age, sex and type of vaccine. For the same subjects we also have the registry with hospital discharge diagnoses, which occurred after the date of vaccination, and there is a personal identifier common to both registers. Indicate which of these studies would be possible to carry out using only the aforementioned sources of information:

options.opa: An analytical cohort study to determine if vaccination increases the risk of developing Guillain-Barré syndrome in the first 16 weeks after influenza vaccination.
options.opb: A descriptive analysis to estimate the incidence of acute myocardial infarction in the first 16 weeks after anti-flu vaccination.
options.opc: A descriptive analysis to estimate the incidence of fever in the first week after the influenza vaccination.
options.opd: A clinical trial that compares the risk of serious post-vaccine reactions (involving hospital admission) with two of the types of influenza vaccines used in that campaign.
options.ope: A case-control study to determine if vaccination increases the risk of developing an acute myocardial infarction.

CHAIN: "Registry of vaccinated subjects" -> "Hospital discharge diagnoses" -> "Identify cases of acute myocardial infarction" -> "Calculate incidence rate" -> "Descriptive analysis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Registry of vaccinated subjects" -> "Hospital discharge diagnoses" -> "Identify cases of fever" -> "Calculate incidence rate" -> "Descriptive analysis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Registry of vaccinated subjects" -> "Hospital discharge diagnoses" -> "Identify serious post-vaccine reactions" -> "Compare reactions between vaccine types" -> "Clinical trial" -> "Not possible with observational data" -> 20%

CHAIN: "Registry of vaccinated subjects" -> "Hospital discharge diagnoses" -> "Identify cases of acute myocardial infarction" -> "Select controls without myocardial infarction" -> "Compare vaccination status" -> "Case-control study" -> 80%

For option opa, an analytical cohort study is feasible as the registry allows for tracking vaccinated individuals and identifying cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome through hospital discharge diagnoses. This aligns with cohort study methodology, which compares outcomes in exposed (vaccinated) vs. unexposed groups. For option opb, a descriptive analysis to estimate the incidence of acute myocardial infarction is possible, as the data allows for identifying cases and calculating incidence rates. Option opc is also feasible, as the registry can identify cases of fever post-vaccination, allowing for incidence calculation. Option opd is not possible, as clinical trials require randomization and controlled conditions, which cannot be achieved with observational data. Lastly, option ope is feasible as a case-control study, where cases of myocardial infarction can be compared to controls without the condition, using vaccination status as the exposure variable.
